Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the all-important run chase! The umpires are back out in the middle and the players of South Africa Under-19 too make their way out after huddling up around the ropes. It will be the pair of Adarsh Singh and Arshin Kulkarni to open the innings for India Under-19. Kwena Maphaka has the new ball in hand as expected and is raring to go. Let's play...
... The Run Chase ...

India Under-19 have bowled fantastically throughout the tournament and they kept up to their performance in this game also. They didn’t allow the openers to go all guns blazing and Raj Limbani made sure that they got 2 wickets within the first powerplay. After that, the spinners kept the batter quiet throughout the middle phases and didn’t allow them to score as many runs as they might have expected. Musheer Khan clinched the wicket of Lhuan-dre Pretorius just when he was about to switch gears followed by the wicket of Oliver Whitehead as well. Dewan Marais fell prey to Saumy Pandey who bowled economically today as well. Naman Tiwari made sure that Richard Seletswane didn’t start hitting boundaries and sent him back to the pavilion. Raj Limbani got rid of the skipper and put South Africa Under-19 in a tough spot. They conceded a few boundaries towards the end but they managed to keep the opposition under 250. The target for them is 245 and with the batting lineup India Under-19 have, it is achievable. Join us back in a bit for the exciting run chase.

Richard Seletswane is up for a chat. He says the idea was to take it deep and he knew it would get easier in the last 10 overs. Adds that he told himself to stay patient and says that with the others going nicely, he took advantage of that. Finishes by saying that the total on the board is a good one and they can defend it.

244 is the score that South Africa Under-19 managed to put up on the board. South Africa Under-19 put up a strong fight against the bowlers throughout the innings. Steve Stolk had to depart early followed by David Teeger who was dismissed before he could do any damage. Lhuan-dre Pretorius stuck to one end and he made sure that the runs kept coming to add to the board. They were playing it safe in the middle overs until Pretorious lost his wicket. Oliver Whitehead and Dewan Marais were also sent back just as they started to attack. They didn’t score many runs in the middle overs but Richard Seletswane played patiently and started to attack during the death overs along with their skipper, Juan James. Richard Seletswane couldn’t see through the innings and had to depart after scoring 64. Juan James was the next to depart after a small cameo but Tristan Luus and Riley Norton made sure that they ended the innings on a powerful note. They have a good bowling unit and they will have to maintain the pressure on the batters.

A brace to end the first innings and 15 runs come off that final over. Shorter one, slower and dug in over middle and leg. Tristan Luus forces the pul,l without much timing and into the vacant space in front of mid-wicket. The bowler has to chase that one down himself and the batters hustle back for two with ease. South Africa Under-19 finish with 244/7 on the board!

Abhinav Mukund joins him and says that he isn't surprised India decided to bowl first. Adds that the pitch is quite dry but the pacers have had more success and there is a bit more grass on the pitch as well.

Juan James, the captain of South Africa Under-19 says they would have liked to bowl first as well but will now have to bat well. Adds that they want to enjoy it and play for the home crowd. Mentions that they are quite comfortable and have played against this opposition in recent times. Also informs that they have one forced change to the Playing XI.

Mentions they are well-prepared and just want to execute their plans. Informs of one change from the last game.

South Africa Under-19 (Playing XI) - Lhuan-dre Pretorius (WK), Steve Stolk, David Teeger, Richard Seletswane, Dewan Marais, Juan James (C), Oliver Whitehead (In for Romashan Pillay), Riley Norton, Tristan Luus, Nqobani Mokoena, Kwena Maphaka.

TOSS - India Under-19 win the toss and they will BOWL first.

India Under-19 on the other hand have remained perfect so far and haven't dropped a single point en route to the knockouts with a number of individuals stepping up in different games. They have scored 250+ runs in every single game and have breached the 300-run mark on a couple of occasions as well which shows their batting prowess. However, they have batted first in all their games so far and haven't chased which might not be the best thing if they are asked to chase in this crunch game. Musheer Khan certainly will be the one to watch out for but they have plenty of other individuals with both bat and ball who can win the game all by themselves. Can South Africa Under-19 beat the mighty Indians and zoom through to a home final? Or will India Under-19 prove to be simply too powerful for them? We shall find out. Toss and team news in a bit.

South Africa Under-19 come into this match on the back of a huge win against Sri Lanka in their last Super Sixes game and in general, they have been pretty solid with both bat and ball. Their only blemish came in a Group game against England where they lost on the DLS method but other than that, it has been smooth sailing for the hosts. Lhuan-dre Pretorius the wicket-keeper opening batter will be the one to watch out for as he can take the game away right at the top along with the fiery Steve Stolk. They have some quality bowlers as well and Kwena Maphaka even picked up six wickets in the last game and has three five-wicket hauls in the tournament. They will need a group effort though if they are to beat the most in-form side in the competition.

The ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup is now heading to its decisive phase where we have got our four semi-finalists - India, South Africa, Australia, and Pakistan. In the first Semi-Final, India Under-19 will be locking horns with South Africa Under-19 at Willowmoore Park, Benoni. Both teams have showcased exceptional skill and determination throughout the tournament, setting the grounds for a thrilling encounter. India's journey in the tournament has been nothing short of spectacular. Undefeated in all five matches, they have displayed a brand of cricket that is both commanding and composed. Led by the astute captaincy of Uday Saharan, India's batting lineup, spearheaded by the consistent performances of Musheer Khan, has been formidable. With Saharan and Khan leading the charge, India boasts the only two batters to have crossed 300 runs in the tournament. In the Super Six, they first badly humbled New Zealand Under-19 by a 214-run margin. Against New Zealand, India's Musheer Khan's hundred set the tone as they bundled New Zealand for a mere 81 runs, with Saumy Pandey bagging a crucial 4-fer. Their victory against Nepal showcased a commanding batting display, with Saharan and Sachin Dhas scoring centuries each, supported by Pandey's exceptional bowling with another 4-wicket haul. On the other hand, South Africa, despite a solitary loss to England, has been impressive throughout the tournament. Finishing at the top with four wins, they've exhibited resilience and skill in equal measure. Notably, their victories against Zimbabwe and Sri Lanka showcased their depth and adaptability. Against Zimbabwe, Kwen Maphaka's stellar 5-fer and Tristan Luus' 3-wicket haul restricted Zimbabwe to 103, allowing South Africa to chase down the target with ease. Facing Sri Lanka, Lhuan-dre Pretorius' composed 71 and Riley Norton's 41 propelled South Africa to defend 232 convincingly. Maphaka's sensational 6-fer dismantled Sri Lanka's top and middle order, complemented by Norton's 4-fer, as they clinched victory by 119 runs. The battle between India's top-order batsmen and South Africa's pace attack will set the tone for the match. How India's Saharan and Khan negotiate Maphaka's pace and movement early on will be crucial, while South Africa will look to strike early and expose India's middle order. Both teams possess depth in their bowling departments. India's ability to maintain pressure through spin and pace variations will be tested against South Africa's aggressive batting lineup. Similarly, South Africa's bowlers will look to exploit any vulnerabilities in India's batting lineup. The excitement is through the roof as both these star-studded teams fight to confirm their berth in the Finale. It is going to be nothing short of a spectacle and a crunched contest.
